questions.q: A body specially constituted to draft a new constitution for a country is known as a
questions.explanation: A constituent assembly is set up specifically to deliberate on and produce a constitution. A national assembly makes ordinary laws, while the cabinet and judiciary perform executive and judicial functions rather than drafting a national constitution.

questions.q: Under the 1999 Constitution, an ordinary amendment requires approval by the Houses of Assembly of what proportion of the states?
options: a simple majority of the states
questions.explanation: An ordinary amendment must pass the National Assembly by a special majority and be approved by the Houses of Assembly of at least two-thirds of the states. Approval by all states is not the constitutional requirement, and one-third or a simple majority falls below the required threshold.

questions.q: A member of the House of Representatives in Nigeria may lose his seat for defecting to another party unless the defection occurs because
options: he has served only one term in the House
the party that sponsored him has divided or merged with another party
his constituents have passed a vote of confidence in him
he is moving to the party of the President
questions.explanation: The Constitution permits a legislator to change party where there is a division or merger in the party that sponsored the election, or another recognized constitutional circumstance. Moving to the President's party, length of service, or a vote of confidence by constituents does not by itself prevent loss of seat.

questions.q: When the President of Nigeria declines to sign a bill passed by the National Assembly, the action is known as the exercise of
questions.explanation: The Constitution empowers the President to withhold assent to a bill, an executive check commonly called the veto. The prerogative of mercy concerns pardons, judicial review is a court power, and delegated legislation is law-making by bodies to which the legislature has delegated authority.

questions.q: One major reason why Nigeria adopted a federal system at independence was to
options: make the judiciary answerable directly to the President
unite the different ethnic groups while allowing them to manage their local affairs
abolish the governments of the regions and states
concentrate all political power in the central government
questions.explanation: Federalism was chosen to keep a large, plural country together by sharing power between a central government and component units. Concentrating all power, controlling the judiciary through the President, or abolishing regional and state governments would be contrary to federal principles.

questions.q: Nigeria operates a three-tier federal system because governmental powers are shared among the
questions.explanation: In the Nigerian federal structure, the three tiers are the federal government, state governments and local government councils. The executive, legislature and judiciary are branches of government, not tiers of the federation.

questions.q: One advantage of a federal system over a unitary system is that it
options: allows component units to retain their identity and manage local affairs
places all governmental power in a single central authority
ensures uniform laws throughout the country at all times
prevents component units from making their own laws
questions.explanation: A federal system shares power between the central government and component units, enabling states or regions to preserve local identities and handle local matters. A unitary system is more centralised, while the wrong choices describe centralisation rather than federalism.

questions.q: Ngozi was born in Enugu to parents who belong to an indigenous community in Anambra State. Under the Nigerian Constitution, her citizenship status is best described as
options: non-citizenship until she obtains a certificate of origin from Anambra State
questions.explanation: A person is a citizen of Nigeria by birth if born in Nigeria and either parent or grandparent belongs or belonged to an indigenous community in Nigeria. Her state of birth or the need for a certificate of origin does not change that constitutional status.

questions.q: Public opinion is most likely to influence government policy when it is
options: based mainly on rumour and hearsay
kept silent and limited to a few individuals
clear, consistent and expressed through organised channels
questions.explanation: Governments are more likely to respond to public opinion that is known, sustained and coordinated through bodies such as civil society groups, the media and professional associations. Rumour, silence or violence makes opinion difficult to measure and less effective as policy input.

questions.q: A major limitation of public opinion as a guide to government decision-making is that it
options: can only be expressed during elections
may be influenced by propaganda and sectional interests
is always uniform across the whole country
is legally binding on every government
questions.explanation: Public opinion can be shaped by media campaigns, religious or ethnic loyalties and pressure groups, so it may not represent a balanced national interest. It is not always uniform, not legally binding in that general sense, and can be expressed through many non-electoral channels.

questions.q: The 1950 Ibadan Constitutional Conference provided the basis for the adoption of which constitution?
questions.explanation: The Ibadan Conference was held in 1950 to review the Richards Constitution, and its recommendations led to the Macpherson Constitution of 1951. The Clifford Constitution came earlier, while the Lyttleton Constitution came later.

questions.q: A civil servant in Abuja obeys a circular issued by her permanent secretary because the Public Service Rules empower the permanent secretary to issue it. This best illustrates
questions.explanation: Legal-rational authority rests on rules, laws and the offices held by officials rather than on personal qualities or inherited custom. Charismatic authority depends on personal appeal, while traditional authority depends on custom and inheritance.

questions.q: The removal of an unpopular government through free and fair elections is best described as an expression of
questions.explanation: Popular sovereignty means that ultimate political authority belongs to the people, and elections are a way through which they exercise it. Parliamentary sovereignty refers to the legislature having final law-making power, while judicial supremacy refers to dominance by the courts.

questions.q: Who was Nigeria's first military Head of State?
options: Major General J. T. U. Aguiyi-Ironsi
questions.explanation: Major General J. T. U. Aguiyi-Ironsi took over as Nigeria's first military Head of State after the January 1966 coup. General Yakubu Gowon succeeded him after the July 1966 counter-coup.

questions.q: The National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) was introduced in Nigeria during the administration of
questions.explanation: The NYSC was established in 1973 under General Yakubu Gowon to promote national unity after the civil war. General Ibrahim Babangida is associated with later programmes such as the Structural Adjustment Programme.

questions.topic: Separation of powers and checks and balances
questions.q: A commissioner in Kano State who continues to sit as a member of the State House of Assembly while serving in the executive is contravening the principle of
questions.explanation: In a presidential system, membership of the executive and the legislature is expected to be distinct, so one person should not serve in both branches at the same time. Checks and balances refers to mutual oversight among the branches, not the combining of offices in one person.

questions.q: Nigeria’s recognition of the MPLA government in Angola in the 1970s was mainly intended to
options: gain immediate oil concessions for Nigerian firms in Angola
prevent Angola from joining the Organisation of African Unity
support African liberation and counter South African influence in Angola
secure a permanent seat for Nigeria on the United Nations Security Council
questions.explanation: Nigeria under Murtala and Obasanjo supported African liberation movements and opposed apartheid South Africa, which backed rival groups in Angola. The recognition was not primarily for a UN Security Council seat or immediate commercial concessions.

questions.q: A Nigerian delegation attends an ECOWAS summit and announces relief materials for a member state hit by floods. This action best illustrates Nigeria’s commitment to
options: exclusive trade with only English-speaking states
questions.explanation: The action is carried out through ECOWAS, a regional body, so it reflects cooperation and humanitarian assistance. Isolationism means withdrawal from international affairs, while exclusive trade would conflict with ECOWAS membership.

questions.q: Traders in Aba close their stalls for two days to press the state government to reduce market levies. This action is best described as
options: a political party holding a primary election
an electoral commission conducting a referendum
a pressure-group method using economic boycott
a local government performing a civic-education function
questions.explanation: Pressure groups use methods such as strikes and boycotts to influence government policy without seeking political office. Closing stalls to force a policy change is an economic boycott, not an election or referendum.

questions.q: During a class debate on Nigeria’s Second Republic, a student is asked to name the party whose presidential candidate, Shehu Shagari, won the 1979 election. The party is the
questions.explanation: The National Party of Nigeria won the 1979 presidential election with Shehu Shagari as its candidate. The Unity Party of Nigeria and the Nigerian People’s Party were strong rivals but did not win the presidency.

questions.q: A pressure group in Abuja campaigns for increased funding of public universities. Its main objective is to
options: contest the presidency under its own platform
win seats in the National Assembly
questions.explanation: A pressure group seeks to influence government decisions rather than capture political office. Contesting elections is the work of political parties, while voter registration is an electoral commission function.

questions.q: In a cabinet system, the principle of collective responsibility requires that
options: the legislature appoints all permanent secretaries
each minister acts without consulting other ministers
the judiciary participates in cabinet meetings
ministers publicly support cabinet decisions or resign
questions.explanation: Collective responsibility means cabinet decisions are jointly owned, so a minister who cannot support them should resign. It does not mean that each minister acts independently or that the judiciary joins cabinet meetings.

questions.q: The main purpose of the doctrine of separation of powers is to
options: allow judges to organise and contest elections
prevent excessive power from being concentrated in one arm of government
give traditional rulers control over the legislature
make the executive superior to the legislature and judiciary
questions.explanation: Separation of powers divides state authority among the executive, legislature and judiciary so that no single arm becomes too powerful. It does not make one arm superior or give traditional rulers control of the legislature.

questions.q: The process by which the Independent National Electoral Commission reviews and adjusts constituency boundaries after a population census is called
questions.explanation: Delimitation is the review and adjustment of constituency boundaries to reflect population changes. Franchise refers to the right to vote, a plebiscite is a direct vote on an issue, and collation is the gathering of election results.

questions.q: Under the alternative vote system, if no candidate wins an absolute majority of first-preference votes, the candidate with the fewest first-preference votes is eliminated and
options: the second-preference votes on the eliminated candidate’s ballots are transferred to the remaining candidates
the candidate with the highest first-preference votes is declared the winner immediately
the election is cancelled and all candidates must wait for a fresh registration of voters
the electoral commission selects the winner from the remaining candidates
questions.explanation: The alternative vote is a preferential system in which low-ranked candidates are eliminated and their ballots are transferred according to voters’ next preferences. This process continues until a candidate obtains an absolute majority, rather than automatically declaring the first-preference leader the winner.

questions.q: The Secretary-General of the United Nations is appointed by the General Assembly on the recommendation of which organ?
questions.explanation: Under the UN Charter, the General Assembly appoints the Secretary-General on the recommendation of the Security Council, where the permanent members may exercise a veto. The Economic and Social Council coordinates economic and social matters, while the International Court of Justice hears legal disputes between states.

questions.q: Which institution carries out the day-to-day administration and technical work of the Economic Community of West African States?
options: Authority of Heads of State and Government
questions.explanation: The ECOWAS Commission, headed by its President, handles the daily administration and technical implementation of community decisions. The Authority of Heads of State and Government gives overall political direction, while the Community Court of Justice adjudicates disputes.

questions.q: Under the African Union Constitutive Act, a decision to intervene in a member state in grave circumstances such as genocide is taken by which body?
options: African Commission on Human and Peoples' Rights
questions.explanation: The Constitutive Act permits the Union to intervene in a member state in grave circumstances, but the power of decision is vested in the Assembly of the Union. The Peace and Security Council recommends and manages peace operations, while the Pan-African Parliament is mainly advisory.

questions.q: Which legislative chamber screens and confirms ministerial nominees submitted by the President of Nigeria?
options: A joint sitting of the National Assembly
questions.explanation: Ministerial nominees are sent to the Senate for screening and confirmation before they can assume office. The House of Representatives does not perform this confirmation role, and the Council of State is an advisory body rather than a legislative chamber.

questions.q: Which of the following is a constitutional check on the President's power over public funds in Nigeria?
options: The President may order the Accountant-General to disregard appropriation once estimates are prepared.
Public funds cannot be spent without appropriation by the National Assembly.
The President must obtain the leave of the Supreme Court before releasing funds to states.
The President can authorise spending from the Consolidated Revenue Fund whenever the budget is delayed.
questions.explanation: The Constitution requires public revenue to be paid into designated funds and spent in line with appropriations made by the legislature. This gives the National Assembly control over the purse and prevents arbitrary spending. Requiring Supreme Court leave or allowing spending without appropriation would undermine legislative control and is not the constitutional position.

questions.q: Which statement best explains the doctrine of judicial precedent in Nigeria?
options: Decisions of higher courts are generally binding on lower courts in similar cases.
Only decisions made during election petitions bind all courts.
Every High Court decision automatically binds the Supreme Court.
A court may ignore earlier decisions of higher courts whenever it disagrees with them.
questions.explanation: Judicial precedent means that a court applies principles laid down in earlier decisions of superior courts to similar cases. In the hierarchy of courts, lower courts are bound by decisions of higher courts, while a court is not bound by a lower court's decision. Disagreement alone does not justify departure where a binding precedent applies.

questions.q: Which of the following matters falls under the exclusive legislative list in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: The exclusive legislative list contains matters reserved for the Federal Government, and currency and coinage is one of them. State universities and local markets fall within state or concurrent arrangements, while market tolls are associated with local government functions.

questions.q: To which account are allocations due to local government councils from the Federation Account and state government paid before distribution in each state?
options: Consolidated Revenue Fund of the Federation
questions.explanation: The Constitution requires each state to maintain a State Joint Local Government Account into which allocations to local governments from the Federation Account and from the state are paid. The funds are then distributed to the local government councils in line with constitutional and statutory provisions. The Federation Account Allocation Committee shares Federation Account revenue among the three tiers; it is not the state-level account for local governments.

questions.q: A child is born in Kano to parents who are citizens of Ghana, and neither the parents nor any grandparent is a Nigerian citizen. What is the child's citizenship status under Nigerian law at birth?
options: The child is a Nigerian citizen by birth because the birth occurred in Nigeria.
The child is not a Nigerian citizen by birth.
The child automatically becomes a Nigerian citizen once the birth is registered in Kano.
The child is automatically a dual citizen of Nigeria and Ghana at birth.
questions.explanation: Citizenship by birth in Nigeria requires a link to a Nigerian citizen or, for persons born before independence, the prescribed indigenous community connection. Mere birth in Nigeria to non-Nigerian parents without the required Nigerian parent or grandparent does not confer citizenship by birth; registration may be relevant to other modes of acquiring citizenship. This is why the child is not automatically a Nigerian citizen by birth.

questions.q: The introductory part of a constitution which states the ideals, aspirations and general purposes of the state is referred to as the
questions.explanation: The preamble introduces a constitution and sets out the guiding ideals and purposes of the state. A schedule contains detailed provisions, while an amendment is a formal alteration to the constitution.

questions.q: The section of a constitution that protects citizens against arbitrary arrest, torture and unlawful detention is commonly known as the
options: fundamental objectives and directive principles of state policy
questions.explanation: A bill of rights, often contained in a chapter on fundamental human rights, protects specific personal freedoms that citizens can enforce in court. Fundamental objectives and directive principles guide state policy, but they are generally not enforceable in the same way.

questions.q: Who was the first Prime Minister of Nigeria under the 1960 Independence Constitution?
questions.explanation: Sir Abubakar Tafawa Balewa led the independence government as Prime Minister from 1960 until 1966. Dr Nnamdi Azikiwe served as Governor-General and later as President, while the other named leaders were regional premiers.

questions.q: The 1958 Constitutional Conference in London was important in Nigeria’s constitutional development because it
options: fixed 1 October 1960 as the date for Nigeria’s independence
introduced the office of the Governor-General
approved the establishment of the Nigerian National Assembly
questions.explanation: The 1958 conference agreed that Nigeria would attain independence on 1 October 1960. The Mid-Western Region was created later, and the office of Governor-General already existed before 1958.

questions.q: A government that has effective control over the territory of a state but lacks constitutional or legal basis is best described as
questions.explanation: A de facto government exercises actual control even though it may not have lawful authority. A de jure government is legally established, while legitimacy refers to acceptance by the people.

questions.q: The principle that ultimate political power belongs to the people is known as
questions.explanation: Popular sovereignty locates final political authority in the people, who express it through elections and consent. Parliamentary sovereignty refers to the legal supremacy of the legislature, not the ultimate power of the people.

questions.q: A government may be legal but lack legitimacy when it
options: controls the police and armed forces
follows constitutional procedures but is widely rejected by the people
prints and issues the national currency
questions.explanation: Legality concerns conformity with the law, while legitimacy concerns the people’s acceptance of the government’s right to rule. Effective control of force, foreign recognition or control of currency does not by itself make a government accepted by its citizens.

questions.q: The two political parties, the Social Democratic Party (SDP) and the National Republican Convention (NRC), were created during the military administration of
questions.explanation: The Babangida administration created the Social Democratic Party and the National Republican Convention as part of its transition programme. Later military governments introduced different political arrangements.

questions.topic: Separation of powers and checks and balances
questions.q: Why is the doctrine of separation of powers considered important in a constitutional democracy?
options: It makes the executive responsible for conducting elections.
It ensures that all public officials belong to the ruling party.
It prevents one branch of government from concentrating and abusing power.
It allows the judiciary to make laws when the legislature is slow.
questions.explanation: The doctrine divides governmental functions among the executive, legislature and judiciary and equips each branch to check the others, so power is not concentrated. It does not require officials to belong to one party, allow courts to make laws, or place election conduct under the executive.

questions.topic: Separation of powers and checks and balances
questions.q: In Nigeria, the Senate invites the Minister of Works to explain why the rehabilitation of a road in Bauchi has stalled. This action is an example of
questions.explanation: Inviting a minister to explain a stalled project is a way for the legislature to scrutinise and hold the executive accountable. It is not judicial review, delegated legislation or an application of federal character.

questions.topic: Separation of powers and checks and balances
questions.q: A High Court in Ibadan declares a state law invalid because it conflicts with the Constitution. This exercise of power is best described as
questions.explanation: Judicial review is the power of courts to examine laws and actions against the Constitution and declare them invalid when inconsistent. Judicial immunity protects judges from suit, while delegated legislation and prerogative writs are different concepts.

questions.q: The principle of sovereign equality of states in Nigeria’s foreign policy means that Nigeria
options: allows foreign states to determine its domestic policies.
accepts the permanent members of the UN Security Council as superior in all matters.
recognises only African states as having legitimate governments.
treats every sovereign state as equal under international law, regardless of size or power.
questions.explanation: Sovereign equality means that states have equal legal standing in international law even though their actual power differs. It does not make large powers legally superior, restrict recognition to African states, or allow foreign control of domestic policy.

questions.q: Nigeria’s membership of the Organisation of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) mainly serves the foreign policy objective of
options: securing automatic admission into the Commonwealth.
obtaining military assistance from oil-importing countries.
promoting cocoa exports among member states.
coordinating oil production policies to protect national revenue and influence global oil prices.
questions.explanation: OPEC is a producers’ organisation through which member countries coordinate petroleum policies in order to stabilise markets and protect oil revenue. It is not concerned with cocoa exports, Commonwealth admission, or military assistance from oil importers.

questions.q: Which of the following is a common criticism of pressure groups in Nigeria?
options: Some pursue narrow interests that may not serve the general welfare.
They are funded exclusively by the Independent National Electoral Commission.
They always contest elections under party platforms.
They are legally barred from peaceful protests.
questions.explanation: A frequent criticism is that pressure groups may promote the interests of a small section rather than the general welfare. Pressure groups do not normally sponsor candidates, are not funded by INEC, and may use peaceful protests.

questions.q: In the Nigerian House of Representatives, the main duty of a party whip is to
options: preside over debates in the chamber.
ensure party members attend sittings and vote in line with the party’s position.
audit the campaign accounts of political parties.
questions.explanation: Whips maintain party discipline by ensuring members are present for important votes and follow the party’s agreed position. Presiding over debates belongs to the Speaker or presiding officer, while voter registration and auditing party accounts are not whip duties.

questions.q: A political party that seeks to win support from all sections of the electorate by adopting broad programmes rather than restricting itself to one class is best described as
questions.explanation: A catch-all party appeals to a wide range of social groups by adopting broad programmes rather than representing only one class or section. Cadre and revolutionary parties are classified on different bases, and a single-issue pressure group is not a political party.

questions.q: A system in which citizens elect representatives to make laws and policies on their behalf is known as
questions.explanation: In a representative democracy, citizens choose representatives who make laws and policies on their behalf. Direct democracy involves citizens deciding directly, while theocracy and autocracy are not based on elected representation.

questions.q: In a ward in Ogun State, 64,000 voters were registered. During the claims and objections exercise, 4,000 names were removed from the register, and 45,000 valid votes were cast on election day. What was the voter turnout as a percentage of the final register?
questions.explanation: The final register is 64,000 - 4,000 = 60,000. Turnout is 45,000 ÷ 60,000 × 100 = 75%. The 70.3% figure results from wrongly using the original register of 64,000.

questions.q: Under the single transferable vote system in a multi-member constituency, a candidate is declared elected when he
options: reaches the quota required for election through first-preference votes or transfers
is endorsed by the largest political party in the constituency
secures an absolute majority at a second ballot
wins more first-preference votes than any other candidate
questions.explanation: Under the single transferable vote, a candidate is elected once the total vote, including transferred preferences, reaches the required quota. Merely leading in first-preference votes or being endorsed by a large party does not guarantee election.

questions.q: Musa uses the Permanent Voter Card of his elder brother, Sani, to cast a ballot at a polling unit in Kano. This act is best described as
questions.explanation: Casting a ballot with another person's Permanent Voter Card is impersonation because the voter falsely presents himself as the registered owner of the card. Multiple voting involves voting more than once, while vote buying involves offering money or favours to influence voting.

questions.q: The Panel of the Wise of the African Union is mainly responsible for
options: settling boundary disputes between member states
appointing the Chairperson of the African Union Commission
advising the African Union on conflict prevention and resolution
questions.explanation: The Panel of the Wise is part of the African Union's peace and security architecture and advises on conflict prevention, mediation and resolution. It does not make binding laws, appoint the African Union Commission head, or act as the primary court for boundary disputes.

questions.q: The Parliament of the Economic Community of West African States is best described as a body that
options: manages the Community's common external tariff
serves as a forum for consultation and dialogue among representatives of member states
makes laws directly binding on citizens of member states
appoints the judges of the ECOWAS Court of Justice
questions.explanation: The ECOWAS Parliament is a consultative and advisory body that brings together representatives to discuss community issues and promote integration. It does not enact laws that directly bind citizens, appoint judges of the Community Court, or manage the common external tariff.

questions.q: In the administration of a Nigerian federal ministry, the Permanent Secretary is best described as
options: the chief administrative officer who advises the minister and oversees the ministry's staff
the elected head of the ministry in the House of Representatives
the officer responsible for interpreting the Constitution in the ministry
a political office holder appointed solely on party strength
questions.explanation: A Permanent Secretary is the chief administrative officer in a ministry and gives continuity in administration by advising the minister and overseeing the civil servants. The position is filled through the public service rather than being an elected or purely party-political post.

questions.q: The Federal Government and Lagos State jointly fund the repair of a busy federal road in the state. This arrangement best illustrates
questions.explanation: Joint funding of a road by the Federal Government and a state government shows the levels of government working together, which is the essence of cooperative federalism. It is not a confederation, a unitary system, or a demonstration that only the federal level has authority in the matter.

questions.q: A state law and a federal law deal with a matter on the concurrent legislative list, but their provisions conflict. Which principle applies in Nigeria?
options: The federal law prevails and the state law becomes void to the extent of the conflict
The matter is automatically removed from the concurrent list
Both laws continue to operate and citizens may choose which to obey
The state law prevails because it operates within the state
questions.explanation: On a concurrent legislative matter, both levels may legislate, but where the laws conflict the federal law prevails and the state law is void only to the extent of the inconsistency. The state law is not completely invalidated, and citizens cannot choose which conflicting law to obey.

questions.q: A polling firm in Jos spends ₦500,000 to interview only 150 traders in one market and presents the results as the opinion of all Plateau State residents on the proposed ban on commercial motorcycles. The main weakness of the exercise is that the
options: results were published by a private firm
proposed ban affects only traders in the market
respondents were asked too many questions
sample is not representative of the state population
questions.explanation: The respondents were selected from one occupational group in one market, so their views cannot be taken as the opinion of the whole state. A credible opinion survey needs a representative sample of the relevant population.
